en: Mount Mayon in Albay province is famous for having the most perfectly symmetrical cone shape of any active volcano.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Luzon Strait.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its entire brain to help it hunt at night.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second largest lake in the Philippines and generates most of the hydroelectric power for the region.
The Philippines is the top global producer of abaca, a banana plant whose strong fibers are woven into ropes and traditional textiles.
Boracay Island in Aklan features White Beach, a four-kilometer stretch of powdery white sand that consistently ranks among the best beaches globally.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines and serves as a natural habitat for the critically endangered Philippine eagle.
The Philippine Trench, located in the Philippine Sea, is the deepest oceanic trench in the country, reaching depths of over 10,500 meters.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected UNESCO World Heritage site sheltering over 600 species of fish.
Located in the Pacific typhoon belt, the Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones annually, which are closely monitored by PAGASA.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching over 400 kilometers and containing the famous Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous ancestors over 2,000 years ago to cultivate staple rice crops.
